summary: contributor_tools/adapters/um21_sign_adapter.py wires UM21 treadmill recordings to sign_application.run_sign_application, one recording and leg at a time. It refuses the six recordings excluded by D-UM21-T02-1 = A before touching any data, and refuses to run unless the backlog still records answer A. It reads untransformed component-1 channels, converting deg to rad only (moments and powers as stored, float64), with the same bounded reading and evidence as probe_core04_um21.py. It calls the hook with dataset UM21, the recording id and the declared detector sha256. Only after the hook does it derive thigh, shank and foot (derive_segment_angles) and the pelvis, thigh, shank and foot sagittal velocities (derive_angular_velocities, spacing = stride duration / 149) from the published channels. It passes no segment angle or velocity to the hook and checks that (F2). contributor_tools/run_core11_um21_pilot.py has two steps. 'plan' wrote docs/quality/audits/core11-p-um21-pilot-spec.json, validated in-process. 'run' is the launched job: it refuses outside the launcher's niceness and address-space limit, writes only under a new output root, and ends with automated pilot checks and pilot_summary.json.

design.hook_inputs: pelvis_tilt, hip/knee/ankle angle (jointAngles <side><Name>Angles component 1, deg -> rad), hip/knee/ankle moment (jointMoments component 1, N*m/kg as stored), hip/knee/ankle power (jointPowers first filled component, W/kg as stored). Pelvis per leg from that side's PelvisAngles, as the CORE-04 probe.
design.F2: No segment angle and no *_velocity channel is read from Streaming.mat, the UM21 MATLAB converters or reconvert_umich_streaming.py; apply_leg raises if one is passed. Segment angles come from derive_segment_angles on the hook's published channels. Velocities come from derive_angular_velocities on the published pelvis tilt and those segments. A held pelvis yields no pelvis velocity and no segments, and the reasons are logged.
design.units: Strides: consecutive source heel strikes 50-250 frames apart (UM21-C03 rule), resampled to 150 samples. Unit ids: um21:Streaming/<subject>/Tread/<condition>:<leg>:frames:<a>:<b>. These are not yet the UM21-T01 task-labelled release observations.
design.evidence: As probe_core04_um21.py: sagittal markers (forward axis from heel->toe via the bound detector's forward_axis), GRF on the foot (N), CoP by the UM21-C03 midpoint rule, plate tilt from the README slope with the sign from the heel path (skipped for i0), task, ParticipantDetails body mass, stride durations. Evidence helpers come from the bound detector bytes.

exclusions.rule: Refused with ExcludedRecordingError before any data access. The planner also refuses if the committed UM21-T02 census clock failures differ from this set.

design.adapter_log: Per leg: adapter path and sha256, order, stride rule and frames per unit, unit conversion, source columns, power slots, hook inputs, F2 statement, input hashes, recording and leg facts, exclusion decision, published, held, derived. The hook's own log, review and derivation logs carry the rest.

Spec test requires the layout-2 pick (reproduced independently from the C03 list and the seed), the v2 paths and the absence of the v1 spec.
R2: The adapter reads the layout from the bound UM21-C03 record. The expected slot is 3 for every joint in layout-2 recordings and 1 otherwise. A joint whose first filled slot differs, or that has no filled slot, raises PowerSlotError and the recording fails. The layout and expected slot are logged per leg (adapter_log.power_layout).

Synthetic tests: AB05/i0 stored as layout 2 uses slot 3 for every joint, ankle power is published with +1 and check_group is clean. AB03/i10 stored as layout 1 (C03 says 2) and AB06/i0 stored as layout 2 (C03 says 1) both fail.
recommended: Cross-group items: explain_cross_group marks each item explained or unexplained, and an unexplained item fails the automated outcome. 'Power slots differ' is explained only when the published groups use different slots and each has its slot's audited sign (a forged equal-slot contrast stays unexplained). I also explain a channel held in some groups and published in others, when every held group has a logged hold reason and every published sign matches the truth. That second category goes beyond the reviewer's wording; please confirm or reject it.

Import chain: the runner loads the adapter from its file, and the adapter loads the hook from its file (sys.modules name reused only when it is the same file). No package __init__ runs in the job. A subprocess test confirms that no contributor_tools package and no pandas get imported. The summary records any that did, and the pilot then fails.

Record writer: 'record' step (build_record/write_record, exclusive create). It writes dataset UM21, pilot_task, outcome, launcher_receipt {path, sha256} and bindings identical to the receipt's spec bindings. Outcome is passed only for a clean completed receipt of job CORE-11-P-UM21-pilot-v2 whose bindings all match before and after, whose hashed outputs include this pilot_summary.json, whose bindings include the summary's bound build, and whose summary automated outcome passed. Tested against sign_application.check_pilot_record on a synthetic committed git repo: the good case passes the gate; six bad runs give outcome failed and the gate refuses them.

R3: explain_cross_group now judges each held group with benign_hold, which uses only structured log fields (verdict, detector_sign, exceptions_applied, recording_exceptions.not_released), never the reason text.

A held group explains an item only when (a) the hold comes from a per-recording exception or a not-released channel, or (b) the verdict is not conflict and the detector sign is None or equals expected_sign (powers by their slot). Every published group must also have the audited sign. Anything else is unexplained, and the pilot fails.

Tests on crafted logs (knee_angle published in one leg, held in the other): suggests -1, applies -1, conflict with no sign and conflict with +1 all stay unexplained. Abstain with no sign and suggest +1 are explained. An ankle_power hold is judged against its slot (suggest -1 explained for slot 1, +1 not). An exception hold is explained even when the detector opposes the truth.
R4: build_record requires that the receipt ran the reviewed spec file (default docs/quality/audits/core11-p-um21-pilot-spec-v3.json): the receipt spec_sha256 must equal the file's sha256, and the receipt's spec bindings must equal the file's bindings. The record carries spec {path, sha256}.

Tests: a receipt whose spec dropped the adapter binding (and its before/after entries) gives outcome failed with exactly the bindings problem. A different spec_sha256 gives outcome failed with exactly the sha256 problem. Both are in the gate test too, where check_pilot_record refuses.
